messages:
lia_support: FYI - customer reports sudden p95/p99 latency from EU (frankfurt) since ~05:10 UTC. They see 600-1200ms p95 on /v1/generate and occasional TLS timeouts. Customer provided traceroute and curl.
mina_net: can you paste the traceroute and a timestamp?
lia_support: pasted below (customer: rahul), ts 2026-03-16T05:12:03Z
rahul (quoted): 
> mtr -r -c 5 api.eu.redwood.com
> Start: 2026-03-16 05:12:01 UTC
> HOST: client.example                  Loss%   Snt   Last   Avg  Best  Wrst StDev
> 1.|-- 10.0.0.1                         0.0%     5    0.3   0.4   0.2   0.6   0.1
> 6.|-- 198.51.100.45                   0.0%     5  120.9 125.1 120.0 135.3   5.2
> 7.|-- 203.0.113.12                    0.0%     5  240.2 248.6 238.9 262.1   8.5  <-- big jump after our edge
> 8.|-- api.eu.redwood.com               0.0%     5  250.5 260.3 249.7 279.1  10.4
> 
> curl -w '%{time_connect} %{time_starttransfer} %{time_total}\n' -o /dev/null -s -D - 'https://api.eu.redwood.com/v1/generate' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>'
> 0.250 0.700 1.230

sam_sre: ops-bot alerted for a p99 spike at 05:09 UTC for eu-west-1, I see increased TLS handshake times in the edge metrics. Can we confirm if this is routing or backend overload?
ops-bot: ALERT: eu-west-1 edge_tls_handshake_p99 = 820ms (+360% vs baseline) at 2026-03-16T05:09:45Z. Active POPs: fra1,ams1,par1.
mina_net: traceroute shows hop 7 (upstream transit) adding ~240ms. That smells like an upstream peering degradation or AS path change. Any recent BGP/route updates?
alex_oncall: No infra changes in last 24h from our side. CDNs/GSLB config unchanged. Suggest quick mitigation: shift traffic away from fra1 temporarily (reroute via ams1) and enable aggressive TLS session reuse for incoming requests.
lia_support: customer asked for a temporary fix; they can tolerate a short window. Do we have a playbook for POP reroute?
sam_sre: yes - steps: 1) update gslb weight for fra1 -> 0.2 (rollover to ams1/par1) 2) bump connection timeout to 10s on edge LB for retries 3) enable retry-with-jitter in API gateway for 504s.
mina_net: running a quick check: looking at our BGP telemetry, a partner transit (AS65033) announced a more specific path for prefix 203.0.113.0/24 at 05:08:30Z causing asymmetric hop to go through a higher-latency path. I'll open peering ticket with partner.
ops-bot: TASK CREATED: peering-ticket-7832 with transit provider AS65033 (priority: high).
alex_oncall: Lia, can you notify the customer we have a mitigation plan and expect partial relief in ~10min after GSLB change? Keep them updated.
lia_support: pinged rahul with the plan and ETA. They replied: "thanks — please keep me posted, this impacts live users."
sam_sre: executing gslb weight change now (dry-run step then apply). Will monitor p95/p99 and TLS handshake histogram.
ops-bot: CHANGE: gslb-weight-update fra1 -> 0.2 applied at 2026-03-16T05:18:12Z by sam_sre.
sam_sre: initial telemetry shows p95 dropped from ~600ms -> ~220ms within 90s for affected customers. TLS handshake p99 moved from 820ms -> 190ms.
mina_net: still seeing some tails because of session affinity to fra1 for existing connections; should normalize as sessions drain. Peering provider responded — they're investigating a capacity issue on their transit.
alex_oncall: recommend follow-ups: 1) peering RCA with provider 2) consider geo-weight floor to avoid rapid single-POP dependency 3) add synthetic probes that measure handshake RTT per upstream hop so we can triage earlier.
lia_support: customer confirmed improved performance and will monitor. They asked for postmortem. I'll keep ticket open until provider RCA done. :thumbsup:
sam_sre: noted for incident log and add timeline. I'll export TLS handshake histograms and add to postmortem.
mina_net: pinging provider contact now.
ops-bot: INCIDENT NOTE: mitigation (GSLB reroute) reduced user impact. Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring.
lia_support: closing loop with customer, leaving thread for postmortem additions. Thanks everyone.
